subject: Re: Redwood MSA - proposed approach for yearly slab cap vs contractwide ceiling
messages:
From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@acme.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Reyes <j.reyes@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: ACME redlines on liability caps (MSA + Order Form)

Connor,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attaching our consolidated redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (see attached). Our main open items are around the limitation of liability: ACME cannot accept a contractwide cap at 1x fees for the full term — for a multi-year commitment this leaves us exposed.

High-level asks from our side:
- We need an annualized cap (per 12-months) rather than aggregate over the full term.
- If you insist on a single aggregated cap, we need it to be at least 3x the fees paid in the contract term (or a minimum floor of $1.5M).
- Carveouts: IP infringement, gross negligence and willful misconduct are carved out; we do not accept carveouts for regulatory fines unless explicitly stated.
- Consequential damages: retain exclusion, but we need clearer language around downstream third-party indemnities.

Please review ACME_Redlines_MSA.docx and let me know your internal position. We need to get to a commercial compromise to keep the procurement timeline on track — target signature by mid-December.

Attachments: ACME_Redlines_MSA.docx, ACME_OrderForm_Redline.xlsx

Best,
Emma
Emma Clark
Senior Counsel, Procurement
ACME Corp

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME redlines on liability caps (MSA + Order Form)

Emma — thanks for sending and for the clear asks. Looping in Laura (legal) and Marcus (account lead) so we can get legal + commercial aligned before returning a redline.

Preliminary internal position (commercial view):
- Redwood needs a predictable exposure in the event of a large claim. Our standard position is either: (A) aggregate cap equal to total fees paid during the term, or (B) annual cap equal to fees paid in a 12-month rolling window, multiplied by a configurable factor for enterprise customers.
- For enterprise deals, we can consider a 2x annualized cap (instead of 1x annual) as a middle ground. Moving to 3x aggregate for the whole term is a large ask — would like to understand ACME's rationale for a 3x multiplier vs 2x annual.
- Carveouts: we can accept IP infringement and willful misconduct carveouts. For regulatory fines and penalties we need to limit carveouts to the extent required by law; we cannot broadly assume responsibility for customer regulatory exposures.

Laura — can you propose a focused redline that outlines: (1) annualized cap option (2x fees per 12-month period) and (2) fallback aggregate cap equal to 1.5x fees for the term, plus a definitional clarification on "fees paid" (invoiced vs recognized). Also include a short rationale so we can present to ACME legal.

Marcus — Emily has requested mid-December signature; what's the timeline on procurement for invoices/PO?

Connor
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Clark <emma.clark@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME redlines on liability caps (MSA + Order Form)

Connor / Marcus — draft redline attached (Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a short summary (Liability_Proposal_Summary.pdf). Key points in the redline: 

1) Fees definition: "Fees paid" means amounts actually paid to Redwood under the Order Form during the applicable 12-month period (invoices issued and not reversed).
2) Primary option (preferred): annual cap = 2x Fees Paid in prior 12-month period, calculated on a rolling basis; this provides reasonable exposure control for Redwood while limiting ACME's risk in any given year.
3) Fallback option: if ACME requires an aggregate (term-wide) cap, we propose 1.5x Fees Paid for the entire contract term, with a minimum floor of $250,000 (to avoid de minimis caps on small pilots).
4) Carveouts: carve out for IP infringement, gross negligence, willful misconduct. For regulatory fines, limited carveout only to the extent Redwood is legally obligated (i.e., we exclude liability for customer's pre-existing compliance obligations).
5) Consequential damages: continue to exclude, but add narrow exception for third-party claim indemnity where Redwood's breach directly causes third-party damages and Redwood controls the defense.

Rationale: the 2x annual cap balances risk transfer for a multi-year commitment and keeps unit economics intact. The 1.5x aggregate fallback is an attempt to meet ACME halfway vs their 3x request.

Please confirm you want me to send this version back to ACME or if you prefer a softer commercial offer (e.g., 2.5x annual or 2x annual + higher floor).

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.docx, Liability_Proposal_Summary.pdf

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: John Reyes <j.reyes@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Clark <emma.clark@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME redlines on liability caps (MSA + Order Form)

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the clarity. ACME reviewed Laura's proposal internally with finance and legal. A couple of points and a counterproposal: 

- ACME will accept an annualized structure rather than pure aggregate, provided the annual multiplier is 3x Fees Paid for that 12-month period. Rationale: our business has variable spend and a year can include large seasonal transactions; 2x still leaves material residual risk to our customers.
- If Redwood cannot move to 3x annual, ACME will accept Redwood's 2x annual option only if the fallback aggregate cap is 2x (not 1.5x) and with a $1M minimum floor.
- Carveouts: we appreciate the carveouts list. We will require a specific carveout for regulatory fines to be capped at $250k unless Redwood's actions caused a regulatory proceeding resulting from gross negligence.
- We also request a reciprocal data breach indemnity clause that clarifies responsibility for actual remediation costs (for incidents caused by Redwood).

Timing: procurement can move quickly if we land on 3x annual or the 2x/2x-floor compromise. We're ready to sign shortly after legal confirmation.

John Reyes
Sr. Procurement Manager
ACME Corp

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: John Reyes <j.reyes@acme.com>, Emma Clark <emma.clark@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME redlines on liability caps (MSA + Order Form)

John / Emma — appreciate the constructive counterproposal and the clarity on procurement timing. Recommendation from Redwood: accept the annualized approach with a capped multiplier at 2.5x Fees Paid per 12-month period, combined with a fallback aggregate cap at 1.75x Fees Paid for the full term and a minimum floor of $500,000. 

Why this compromise: 2.5x annual meets ACME closer to its 3x ask while keeping our exposure bounded; 1.75x aggregate fallback preserves predictable worst-case economics and the $500k floor prevents de minimis outcomes on small pilots. We will keep carveouts as previously proposed but can accept your $250k cap carveout for regulatory fines with the gross negligence carveout exception you requested. Laura will produce a clean redline incorporating the 2.5x/1.75x terms and the regulatory carveout cap.

Next steps:
- Laura to issue redline (Redwood_MSA_redline_v4.docx) and a short summary memo by EOD tomorrow.
- Marcus to confirm commercial acceptance and update procurement on the timeline for PO issuance.
- Emma / John: if this is acceptable, please confirm and we'll route a final DocuSign packet.

Connor O'Brien
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
